title_vi: Tám vấn đề thường gặp khi hệ thống lớn lên, và cái giá của từng cách giải

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a git fetch of the pinned commit and hashed as a Git blob; computed OID matches the source map. Non-empty source was read; no source-image bytes used.

claims.evidence: Eight problem/solution pairs from the source body; cache-aside, sharding and CDN statements read from local clones of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at 8e2c239; LSM and synchronous-write statements read from google/leveldb at bb74ef7; five costs measured by Python 3.13.16 programs with sqlite3 and standard-library HTTP servers on a 4-vCPU virtual machine on 2026-10-19 (three or four runs). The toy LSM is not a real LSM store. Block/object storage and centralized logging have no independent reference here and CDN/large files/logging are not measured.

mobile.evidence: Figure drawn by scripts/figures (viewBox width 320, smallest font 15 px, shown at 13.5 px at 320 px); python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser passed; the lesson (Markdown to HTML, optional sections open, 16 px side gutters) rendered in Chromium at 320, 375 and 430 px with no horizontal overflow of the page, any table or any code block. Not learner testing and not GitHub or a real phone.

claims.claim_vi: Source: eight problems and solutions - read-heavy: cache; high-write: async workers and LSM-tree databases; single point of failure: redundancy and failover; high availability: load balancing and database replication; high latency: CDN; large files: block and object storage; monitoring: centralized logging with the ELK stack; slow queries: indexes and sharding.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft cache-aside: load on demand, on write update the store and invalidate the cached item, no guarantee of consistency, a reader may briefly see stale data.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft sharding: the shard key is the most critical decision and changing it needs data migration; queries on attributes outside the shard key can use the Index Table pattern.
claims.verified_by: Read from the same local clone.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft CDN guidance: edge servers close to users minimise latency, typically for static content; the CDN is a potential single point of failure.
claims.verified_by: Read from the same local clone.

claims.claim_vi: leveldb: updates go to a log file and an in-memory memtable, are converted to sorted tables in levels and merged by compaction; asynchronous writes are often more than a thousand times as fast as synchronous writes, and a WriteBatch amortises the cost of one synchronous write.
claims.section: Log files; Sorted tables; usage guide Synchronous Writes
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of google/leveldb at commit bb74ef739973a70ca9f0d90788a1da89b788c0ad (doc/impl.md and doc/index.md).

claims.claim_vi: Cache test: sqlite3 file with 100,000 keys, 200,000 reads with Zipf exponent 1.1 (fixed seed), LRU cache: hit rate 0/45/66.4/83% for cache of 0/0.1/1/10% of the data; mean read 4.9-5.8, 3.5-4.6, 2.0-3.3, 1.2-1.9 microseconds; a write without invalidation leaves a stale value.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19 (three runs).

claims.claim_vi: Write test: 100,000 random keys; sqlite3 synchronous=FULL one commit per insert (10,000 inserts) 6.1-7.5 thousand per second; append-only log plus in-memory table with fsync after each record (10,000) 5.2-6.3 thousand; fsync every 1,000 records 0.48-0.79 million; sqlite3 synchronous=OFF batch of 1,000 0.37-0.49 million; log plus memory without fsync 0.75-1.2 million (2.0-2.7 times the sqlite3 batch run in the same run); toy LSM point read 5.6 microseconds over 9 runs and 1.4 after merging into one run (one run).
claims.verified_by: Programs run by the author on 2026-10-19 (three runs); toy structures, not a real LSM store.

claims.claim_vi: Index/shard test: sqlite3 in memory, 400,000 rows: count by user 13-15 ms without index and 6.6-8.1 microseconds with; loading 400,000 rows 24, 51, 99 and 142 percent slower with the index in four runs; 8 shards by user: query on the shard key 7-11 microseconds, range query on another column asking all shards 25-42 against 13-22 on one database.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19 (four runs); one process, no parallelism.

claims.claim_vi: Load-balancing test: three local HTTP servers, one stopped, 300 requests round robin: 200 succeeded without health checks, 297 with a passive check that removes a backend after 3 consecutive failures (three runs); availability of k copies with instant failover 1-(1-a)^k, simulated 500,000 times.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19 (three runs).

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: tám cặp của nguồn, năm cái giá đo được, ba cặp chưa đo.
source_deviations: The source is a picture with eight one-line pairs; the lesson keeps the eight pairs in order, adds a cost column and measures five of them.
The LSM structure measured is a toy, the databases are in-process, and CDN, large files and centralized logging are not measured.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết tại repo này (gói W8), giữ ở trạng thái draft chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
